backers.name: SoftBank Group Corp.
backers.note: SoftBank Group (telecom-rooted Japanese technology/investment conglomerate) is the primary sponsor of the Vision Funds; Vision Fund 1 ($98.6B committed) also drew capital from Saudi PIF and Mubadala, while Vision Fund 2 (~$56B) is funded mainly by SoftBank Group itself.

aum.raw: ~$154B combined across Vision Fund 1 (~$98.6B) and Vision Fund 2 (~$56B)

strategy.thesis: The world's largest tech-focused investment platform; maintains a dedicated Life Sciences & HealthTech investment team (led by director John Cassidy) and has been ranked the #2 late-stage digital health investor globally, deploying billion-dollar-scale checks into digital pharmacy, telehealth and mental-health companies.

summary.en: SoftBank Group's ~$154B Vision Fund platform runs a dedicated Life Sciences & HealthTech team; notable health bets include a $1B investment in digital pharmacy Alto Pharmacy (2022, Vision Fund 2) and leading digital-mental-health company Big Health's $75M Series C (2025). Galen Growth ranked it the #2 late-stage digital health investor globally for 2025.

strategy.thesis: Mitsui Chemicals' second corporate VC fund (after 321Force, 2022, managed by Global Brain), roughly double the first fund's size; multi-industry mandate spanning Life & Healthcare, Mobility, ICT and Sustainability, with healthcare investments targeting emerging biotech platforms, drug-delivery systems, regenerative medicine and materials for medical devices.

summary.en: Mitsui Chemicals' second corporate venture fund, launched May 2025 with $60M via new San Jose-based subsidiary 321Catalyst Ventures, Inc.; life sciences/healthcare (biotech platforms, drug delivery, regenerative medicine, medical-device materials) is one of several named priority sectors alongside mobility, ICT and sustainability.
